name: Sulfur plains
basis: Io's bright plains are frost and deposits of sulfur and sulfur dioxide from its volcanoes, the richest sulfur surface known. Grade is relative.

name: Volcanic paterae
basis: Around the lava lakes the surface is silicate lava with sulfur flows on its flanks, less pure than the plains. Grade is relative.

name: Ridged plains
basis: The bulk of Europa's surface is nearly pure water ice, young and ridged, on an ice shell tens of kilometres thick over an ocean. Grade is relative.

name: Chaos terrain
basis: In Tara Regio the ice carries carbon dioxide drawn from the ocean below, with salts, so mixed volatile ice is here and not on the plains. Grades are relative.

name: Bright grooved terrain
basis: Young, clean water ice cut by grooves over about two thirds of Ganymede. Grade is relative.

name: Dark cratered terrain
basis: Old terrain where ice is mixed with dark material and with carbon dioxide and other volatiles. Grades are relative.

name: Cratered plains
basis: Callisto's ancient surface is ice and rock with carbon dioxide ice detected on it. Grades are relative.

name: South polar terrain
basis: Plumes from the tiger stripes carry ammonia at close to 1 percent, carbon dioxide and organics with the water vapour, frozen onto the surface around them. Grades are relative.

name: Atmosphere
basis: A 1.45 bar atmosphere of 95 percent nitrogen. Known from Cassini and Huygens.

name: Northern hydrocarbon seas
basis: Kraken Mare, Ligeia Mare and Punga Mare near the north pole are liquid methane, ethane and nitrogen; radar showed Ligeia to be methane-rich. Grade is relative.
